_comment: The UX programme's five lanes (#558), as a roster rather than a docket.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (#582). finding-propagation.mdc requires a verified finding that
constrains a later stage to be written into that stage's own brief, in the tree, and says an
issue comment is not propagation. Waves 1-5 have that destination; lanes B-F had none, so two
seats tried to comply and had nowhere to write. This is the destination.
Discovered by .claude/workflows/brief_lint.mjs through its wave-*-groups.json glob, which is
why the name carries the wave- prefix even though the lanes are not a wave.
NOT a wave: the five lanes run CONCURRENTLY and are picked up one item at a time. This file is
not launched by web-fix-wave.js as a single group list; `after` edges order items WITHIN a lane
only, and no edge crosses lanes.
Group ids are the docket's own (B1-B12, C1-C4, D1-D6, E1-E4, F1-F2): 28 pull-request units
covering the 34 items, because the docket rules C1 one PR rather than four and folds three
Per-lane cost, from the docket: docs/ is INERT so lane B selects no test script; structure.py
walks *.py only so lane C moves no ratchet metric; lane D is Python outside the coordinator
class; lane E coordinates with the settings registry; lane F is the only lane that adds lines
to coordinator.py, where coordinator_loc and max_class_loc sit at zero headroom.
Numbers in a brief are snapshots. Re-measure at your own merge base; #411 rule 4 refuses a
literal budget figure for exactly this reason.

groups.brief: Regenerate the card screenshot from the existing browser lane, replacing B4's interim asset. THIS BRIEF CARRIES THE HACS IMAGE CONSTRAINTS FOR EVERY FIGURE ITEM IN LANE B, AND CARRIES THEM AS A MECHANISM RATHER THAN AS A LIST OF SHAPES: the constraint has been carried three times and stated too narrowly twice, each restatement enumerating the shapes then known, and each time an ordinary construct satisfying every listed clause still shipped blank. Derive your own case from the mechanism; do not match your figure against the examples. Established by PR #567's review by execution against the pinned markdown and sanitiser versions with HACS's own repository-context markdown helper; the regex behaviour was re-derived independently for #582 by running the recorded expression, and the sanitiser and candidate-file halves are #567's measurement and were not re-derived. THE MECHANISM IS TWO STEPS. One: the rewriter matches \[.*?\]\([^#](?!.*?:\/\/).*?\) -- a bracket-then-parenthesis span whose target must not open with a fragment marker and must fail a negative lookahead for a scheme separator, carrying no dotall flag -- and then replaces THE FIRST OPEN PARENTHESIS OF THE MATCHED SPAN, which is not necessarily the image's, with the raw-content prefix; its companion test for a markdown extension is likewise applied to the whole span rather than to the link. Two: whatever is still relative afterwards is blanked by the sanitiser, which keeps a source only when it is absolute or rooted at a slash, a dot-slash or a dot-dot-slash. EVERY CLAUSE BELOW IS A CONSEQUENCE OF THOSE TWO STEPS, each with the control that separates it from its imitation. The image is inline markdown: the rewriter touches a bracket-parenthesis pair and nothing else, so a reference-style image and raw HTML with a relative source are never rewritten at all and are then blanked; control, the same image written inline survives. The parenthesis opening the source is the FIRST parenthesis in the span: a parenthetical caption takes the rewrite instead, and this is the case every earlier statement of this constraint permitted. Control, a minimal pair: ![Plan chart (24 hours)](docs/img/chart-anatomy.svg) ships blank, while ![Plan chart 24 hours](docs/img/chart-anatomy.svg) is rewritten and renders. The same clause governs a linked image, and the earlier statement attached the consequence to the wrong construction: when an image with a relative source is wrapped in a link, the span's first parenthesis IS the image's own, so its source is rewritten correctly and only the anchor target is left relative; the construction that really mangles a source is a badge whose source is ALREADY ABSOLUTE, which collects the prefix in front of it. The span carries no markdown extension: the rewrite flips to a blob path serving HTML inside an image element, broken rather than blank; control, an alt text naming docs/architecture.md takes the blob path while the same alt text without it reaches raw content and renders. No scheme separator appears later on the line: the lookahead scans to the end of the LINE rather than the end of the link, so a relative image sharing its line with any absolute URL is never rewritten and is then blanked; control, the identical image alone on its line survives. The alt text does not wrap: with no dotall flag a dot cannot cross a newline; the control is that a NEGATED CHARACTER CLASS CAN, so a reconstruction written with a negated class in place of the lazy dot matches the wrapped case, reproduces nothing, and wrongly concludes the constraint is not real. None of this is visible on GitHub, which is where a figure is reviewed, so re-verify by rendering rather than by reading this paragraph. These constraints are README-ONLY: #567's review established that the HACS integration builds its candidate files from a single README stem carrying no path separators, so files under docs/ are never rendered by it and reach the reader through GitHub instead. Do not silently widen these rules to docs/, and do not narrow them away from README.md. PR #567's head states this same mechanism in docs/plan-2026-09-open-issues.md; the two are deliberately one statement in two places, and if they ever disagree the newer is right and the other is the bug.

The refusal is protective and its control is upstream's own behaviour at the floor declared in hacs.json: a sensor carrying an option list raises on EVERY state write whose value falls outside that list, so an option list is a whitelist and not documentation. The first refused sensor publishes the solver's own message text on a branch whose docstring says it fires routinely on a flat price curve, so enumerating it would have taken the entity down in ordinary operation rather than in an edge case; the second emits a two-word state containing a space, which cannot be a translation key at all. Both want the reshaped treatment D6 describes, a bounded companion sensor and a deprecation, never a mutated state. Write no state key for a sensor D3 did not enumerate; an in-tree check already refuses a key falling outside its sensor's options, so this is enforced rather than advised, and re-derive the three option lists at your merge base rather than copying them.

groups.brief: Group the wide options pages, using the grouping construct the flow library provides. TWO ASSUMPTIONS IN THE ORIGINAL FRAMING WERE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED HERE. First, the construct does not live in the selector helpers; it is defined in data_entry_flow.py, and it has existed since well before the floor that was thought to gate it, so the version floor stopped binding earlier than the parking note assumed, although the original parking was correct against the floor current at the time. Second, THE LANE'S REAL COST IS IN THE ASSERTION LAYER RATHER THAN THE CAPTURE. PR #568 taught the config-flow golden's fingerprint to walk nested groups, so the fixture no longer goes silently blind; it groups no page, so #516 stays open. What remains is that the assertion layer walks schemas ONE LEVEL DEEP in many places, and every one of those stops asserting silently on a grouped page rather than failing. #558 counted those walks at a named commit under a stated rule, AST reads of a schema attribute that are iterated or subscripted, excluding schema construction and the getattr-with-default form; RE-DERIVE THE COUNT AT YOUR OWN MERGE BASE under that same rule rather than carrying the figure, and state the rule with whatever number you get. THE FOURTH SEQUENCING RULE, which #558 records alongside its three: a capture must be able to see a change before the change is made. Grouping and fixing the capture in one PR would have moved the fixture once and then silenced it forever, with nothing in the suite able to say so. Split capture from change.
